correctness.rationale: Exact exponential-race conditioning yields (1); two-index Bernoulli identity yields endpoint bounds. For t→0 and nt→∞, m∼1/t, v∼1/(2t); Fourier inversion supplies a uniform O(1/v) adjacent-mass estimate, establishing near-total local mass at k≈m. Uniform convergence of t k e^{-kt} to 1/e on the mass window, a Chebyshev tail bound, and dominated logarithmic integration prove the limit. A standalone checker passes 39 deterministic checks by two independent exact finite implementations. No limiting law is inferred from tests.

value.rationale: The motivating paper gives a concrete unresolved natural fixed-point question in a singular Luce law. The theorem determines the leading scale and sharp coefficient of its expected count, required before assessing any distributional conjecture, with an explanatory Bernoulli mass-localization mechanism. It is not a routine finite table or arbitrary parameter slice; the Sukhatme weights are a named canonical regime and the divergent diagonal density obstructs regular fixed-point arguments.
